registry: npm registry metadata read for 143 of 143 packages

items.title: Lockfile hashes differ from the registry
items.subject: package-lock.json

verified_evidence.fact: Compared the integrity hash of 131 locked packages with the hash the npm registry publishes
75 mismatch: adm-zip@0.4.4, ansi-regex@3.0.0, bcrypt-nodejs@0.0.3, bl@1.0.3, body-parser@1.18.3, ansi-regex@3.0.0, nconf@0.6.9, debug@2.2.0

items.inference: A hash that differs from the registry means the lockfile points at different bytes than the published release: either the lockfile was edited or the package came from somewhere else.
items.remedy: Delete the affected entries, regenerate the lockfile from the registry and investigate who changed it.

items.title: Where every package is downloaded from — non-registry sources found
items.subject: package-lock.json

verified_evidence.fact: Download sources in the lockfile: registry.npmjs.org (963), (bundled) (515), github.com (1)
0 packages have no integrity hash; 646 only have a SHA-1 hash

items.inference: Packages from git URLs, other hosts or without integrity hashes bypass the registry's checks, so a changed upstream repo or a compromised host could swap the code without the lockfile noticing.
items.remedy: Replace git/URL dependencies with registry releases and regenerate the lockfile so every entry has a sha512 integrity hash.

items.title: 2 dependencies accept any future version
items.subject: package.json

verified_evidence.fact: grunt-env: "latest" (devDependencies)
grunt-if: "https://github.com/binarymist/grunt-if/tarball/master" (devDependencies)

items.inference: An unbounded range lets the next published release in automatically; if that release is malicious (a hijacked maintainer account), a fresh install picks it up.
items.remedy: Use a caret or exact range and rely on the lockfile; review upgrades deliberately.

items.title: 3 container images are referenced by tag, not by digest
items.subject: Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml

verified_evidence.fact: node:12-alpine (tag)
node:12-alpine (tag)
mongo:4.4 (tag)

items.inference: Mutable tags can be repointed upstream. A tag such as 'latest' or '24' can be moved to a different image at any time, so two builds of the same commit may ship different operating-system packages.
items.remedy: Pin the image by digest (image@sha256:...) so the same bytes are used every build, and update the digest deliberately.

verified_evidence.fact: 1 lockfile entries resolve outside registry.npmjs.org
node_modules/grunt-if -> https://github.com/binarymist/grunt-if/tarball/master

items.inference: Non-registry sources bypass registry integrity guarantees.
items.remedy: Delete the suspicious entry and regenerate the lockfile from the official registry (npm install --package-lock-only), then compare integrity hashes before merging.

items.title: cypress@3.3.1 runs code when installed (download)
items.subject: cypress@3.3.1

verified_evidence.fact: package-lock.json marks cypress@3.3.1 with hasInstallScript: true
Used in: development only
Install script published on npm: postinstall: node index.js --exec install
Reaches the app through owasp-nodejs-goat@1.3.0 → cypress@3.3.1

items.inference: The install script downloads or unpacks a binary at install time. That binary is not covered by the lockfile's integrity hash, so it is a provenance gap.
items.inference_source: rule-based inference (pattern match on the script text)
items.remedy: Pin the binary version, verify its checksum, and build with --ignore-scripts in CI, allowing scripts only for packages you have reviewed.

items.title: 16 of 16 production dependencies have no build provenance
items.subject: package.json

verified_evidence.fact: 0 direct production dependencies publish an npm provenance attestation (built by CI from a known repo)

Without attestation: bcrypt-nodejs@0.0.3, body-parser@1.18.3, consolidate@0.14.5, csurf@1.9.0, dont-sniff-mimetype@1.0.0, express@4.16.4, express-session@1.15.6, forever@2.0.0, helmet@2.3.0, marked@0.3.5, mongodb@2.2.36, needle@2.2.4, node-esapi@0.0.1, serve-favicon@2.5.0, swig@1.4.2…

items.inference: A package without provenance was uploaded from someone's machine, so nobody can prove the tarball matches the source repository. That is normal for older packages, but it is the gap attackers use when they steal a maintainer's npm token.
items.remedy: Prefer versions with provenance when upgrading; for critical packages, compare the tarball with the tagged source.

items.title: 4 CI actions not SHA-pinned
items.subject: .github/workflows

verified_evidence.fact: 4 CI actions not SHA-pinned
actions/cache@v2, actions/checkout@v2, actions/setup-node@v1, actions/upload-artifact@v2

items.inference: Tag-pinned actions can be changed by their owners.
items.remedy: Review the action's source, pin it to a full commit SHA, and give the workflow the minimum token permissions it needs.
